subject: Dedicated reservation options and staged onramp — Aurorix discussion
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Grant Morris <grant.morris@aurorix.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation options and staged onramp — Aurorix discussion

Hi Grant —

Thanks again for taking time today. Per our call, attached is a concise set of dedicated reservation options built to match Aurorix's inference profile and sprinted ramp over the next 6 months. High level: we focused on predictable throughput with burst windows and a small warmup credit package to limit cold-start token cost during model tuning.

Attachments: Aurorix_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf (PDF), Prewarm_Credit_T&Cs.pdf (PDF)

Short summary (three options):

1) Option A — Compact Onramp (lowest commit)
- Minimum reserved footprint: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared across model variants)
- Typical steady-state throughput: ~120 reqs/sec (batching dependent)
- Ramp: 8 GPUs baseline -> 12 GPUs month 2 -> 16 GPUs month 4
- Warmup credits: 50k tokens/month for first 3 months
- SLA: 99.5% p95 latency target, standard support

2) Option B — Medium Footprint (balanced economics)
- Minimum reserved footprint: 24x A100-eq GPUs
- Throughput: ~360 reqs/sec with preferred batching profile
- Ramp: 24 -> 40 GPUs across 90 days (heat-up triggers)
- Warmup credits: 150k tokens/month first 3 months
- Includes 2 planned burst windows/month (3x capacity up to 24 hours)

3) Option C — Anchor Slate (aggressive throughput)
- Minimum reserved footprint: 64x GPUs
- Throughput: line-rate enterprise serving (low-latency SLAs)
- Ramp: immediate 64 with phased scaling plan for months 2-6
- Warmup credits: 500k tokens + priority onboarding

Notes on burst and fallbacks: requests above reserved capacity can burst into our shared capacity subject to regional availability; we also support automatic fallback to a smaller/quantized model variant to preserve latency while keeping unit cost bounded.

Next steps I recommend: 1) pick an option to align procurement, 2) we issue a SOW and draft DocuSign, 3) schedule a 30-minute onboarding kickoff with our Platform & CS teams to lock the warmup runbook.

If you'd like, I can propose a softened minimum: we can build Option A' with a 6-GPU starting footprint + a step-up credit schedule as a conservative onramp for first 30 days.

Open to feedback — attaching the short SOW template in case procurement wants to preview contract language.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Aurorix_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf]
[Attachment: Prewarm_Credit_T&Cs.pdf]

From: Grant Morris <grant.morris@aurorix.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and staged onramp — Aurorix discussion

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clear options. A few quick questions so I can loop in procurement and engineering: 

- Can you confirm burst pricing during the 3x capacity windows? Is it billed at list or discounted for reserved customers?
- Our initial experiments suggest we might only need a 4 GPU footprint for the first 2 weeks while models are still tuning. Is there any way to start at 4 GPUs and then backfill to the minimum reservation?
- Is the warmup credit applied at account-level or per-model? We have two concurrent models in test.

Also can you send a rough cost delta between Option A and B (monthly committed charge + expected overage %)? Procurement will want numbers to compare to internal run-rate.

Grant
Grant Morris
CTO, Aurorix Therapeutics
grant.morris@aurorix.com

Date: 2027-10-15T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated reservation options and staged onramp — internal sizing note

Priya — quick internal note on feasibility: we can support a temporary 4-GPU prewarm in a hosted lane (non-reserved) for up to 14 days to keep cost low while the team tunes models. That will be billed as overage but we can apply warmup credit against it. For the 3x burst windows, recommend we cap max concurrent burst at +25% of reserved for the first 90 days to avoid regional capacity pressure; beyond that we can enable runway bursts (3x) per the plan if inventory allows.

I'll draft a short paragraph for the SOW that codifies burst discount (15% off list for reserved customers during burst windows) and the prewarm transitional lane.

K
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Grant Morris <grant.morris@aurorix.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-15T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and staged onramp — Aurorix discussion

Grant — thanks for the questions; answers below and a suggested compromise.

- Burst pricing: for reserved customers we apply a burst discount of 15% off list for capacity consumed during the scheduled burst windows. Out-of-window bursts are billed at list but we can set a hard cap via policy to prevent runaway charges. (Kim confirmed this.)

- 4 GPU starter: we can offer a 14-day hosted prewarm lane at 4 GPUs while models tune. The hosted lane consumption will be billed as overage against account usage, but we will apply the warmup credits you choose (e.g., 50k tokens) to offset first-month consumption. After 14 days, the reservation must be activated to meet the minimum committed footprint unless we agree to an Option A' (6 GPU minimum) with a short ramp schedule: 6 -> 8 -> 12 over 30 days.

- Warmup credit scope: applied at the account level, and it can be split between model IDs. We will flag the two model ids you specify so credits are correctly apportioned.

Cost delta (high level, illustrative):
- Option A (8 GPUs): $38k/month committed + expected 10–15% overage in month 1 if heavy tuning
- Option B (24 GPUs): $110k/month committed + expected 3–5% overage
(Precise numbers in the attached PDF; these are estimates for procurement to compare run-rate.)

Proposed compromise for immediate go:
- Start: 14-day hosted prewarm at 4 GPUs (covered by warmup credits)
- Onboarding trigger: Day 12 we finalize paperwork; reservation activation Day 15
- Reservation: Option A' — 6 GPU minimum with step-up to 12 by day 30, then follow Option A ramp thereafter.

If that sounds acceptable I will: 1) update the SOW with the burst discount paragraph (Kim will add the exact clause), 2) send DocuSign with Option A' and the SOW, and 3) schedule an onboarding call with Platform/CS for next-week.

Thanks —
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW_template_AURX.docx]
From: Grant Morris <grant.morris@aurorix.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-16T13:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and staged onramp — Aurorix discussion

Priya — that compromise works for us. Please send the DocuSign for Option A' and the SOW so I can loop in procurement. Two small asks before we sign:

1) Can procurement have a single procurement contact on your side for PO/SOW questions?
2) Can you include a one-paragraph rollback clause (30-day notice, ability to step down commit size by 50% with 60-day lead) — procurement needs explicit off-ramp language.

Once procurement signs we can target activation on Oct 31 so we line up with our sprint.

Grant
